title: Cohomology is computed after hypercover refinement
statement:
For a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme $X$, an abelian etale sheaf $F$,
and $q\geq0$, there is a natural isomorphism

$$
 \varinjlim_{U}H^q(C^\bullet(U,F))
 \xrightarrow{\sim} H^q(X_{\Et},F).
$$

The limit is over refinements, modulo simplicial homotopy, of the hypercovers
finite in each degree [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover]. The right side
is the derived cohomology of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. A
representative, and a relation between representatives, use only finitely
many degrees. The same assertion holds for sheaves of modules over a fixed
constant ring, with cohomology derived in that module category.

proof.text: Prove homotopy invariance for every abelian coefficient category. Apply the contravariant section functor to a simplicial homotopy, use Mathlib SimplicialObject.Homotopy.toChainHomotopy on the opposite category, dualize the resulting chain homotopy, and identify the dual alternating face complex with the alternating coface complex. Homotopic cochain maps induce the same homology maps. Extend this equality through the equivalence relation generated by simplicial homotopies.

Apply the module coefficient comparison to the constant ring ULift Z. Its forgetful functor to abelian groups is an additive equivalence, as is the induced functor on etale sheaves (ModuleCat.forget₂_uliftInt_isEquivalence and Etale.isEquivalence_sheafCompose_forget₂_uliftInt). Construct the cochain comparison degree by degree using identity components; additivity identifies the alternating differentials. The homology preservation isomorphism gives a natural coefficient comparison compatible with every refinement.

Identify global sections with evaluation at the terminal etale object to commute global sections with the coefficient equivalence. Use rightDerivedFunctorCompMapDerivedCategoryIso, rightDerivedFunctorNatIso, rightDerivedFunctorCompIso and singleFunctorCompRightDerivedFunctorIso to commute the sheaf cohomology functors with this equivalence. All these comparison isomorphisms are constructed from proved library APIs.

Precompose the module cocone with the inverse equivalence on sheaves, apply the coefficient forgetful functor, and conjugate with the cochain and derived cohomology comparison isomorphisms. Refinement compatibility follows from the cochain comparison and naturality of the sheaf-equivalence counit. Transport pointwise unique factorization explicitly: choose an inverse image of the target abelian group, use fullness to lift each leg, apply the module universal property, and use faithfulness for uniqueness. Combine this abelian colimit property with the independent homotopy-invariance proof and the existing module coefficient clause for each ring.
